title: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink Says $40 Trillion US Debt ‘Will Not Be as Consequential’ If AI Drives 3% GDP Growth
key_facts: Fink told CNBC a data-centre moratorium would mean recession: 'So much of our economy is based on the build-out of this capex'
He said data centres are 'not the problem' and help create jobs amid shortages of electricians, plumbers and welders
He said private capital must be unlocked to grow the economy 3%
National debt rose from $8 trillion in 2000 to $40 trillion
BlackRock is working with hyperscalers and chipmakers on financing based on chips' residual value, taking about a year
BlackRock Q3 EPS $15.93 vs $14.15 expected; assets under management $15.5 trillion
quote_evidence: "If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," Fink said in an interview with CNBC.
"We need to unlock private capital to grow the U.S. economy by 3%," Fink said.
why_it_matters_hint: The world's biggest money manager says AI data centres now hold up US growth.
notes: Benzinga page blocked; read Stocktwits and Cryptopolitan reports of the CNBC interview. The Benzinga headline claim that the debt 'will not be as consequential' if AI drives 3% growth was not found in either text, so the headline here uses the verified points. Interview Wed 14 Oct, after BlackRock's Q3 results.
